claims.claim_text: Joseph P. Verkamp was an engineering student at the University of Cincinnati immediately before entering Army service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: His obituary says he left University of Cincinnati engineering studies to enlist and was later assigned to the OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from exact uncommon name, PFC context, official protected-identifier agreement and explicit obituary OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the last documented civilian status before Army service; the obituary's 1943 year conflicts with the official 1942 entry date.
claims.match_notes: Student status is not employment and is therefore not marked as a last civilian employer. The date conflict is disclosed and not silently reconciled.

claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon exact first and last name, captain context and Greek Operational Group service align with the indexed official record.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence, but the NPS source omits the middle initial and protected identifier; Box 803 remains the final identity check.
claims.temporal_assessment: The NPS account documents wartime OSS operations, not a pre-OSS employer or transfer chronology.
claims.match_notes: No pre-OSS employer is inferred from the operational history.

claims.claim_text: Before later U.S. Army and OSS service, Marcel Verzeano worked as a physician and staffer with the American Rescue Center in Marseille.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Varian Fry Institute identifies Marcel Verzeano as an American Rescue Center staffer and Romanian Jewish doctor involved in refugee rescue.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare exact name, physician description and exact official protected-identifier match to the indexed later officer.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented in Marseille in 1940-1941; the evidence does not establish it as the immediate predecessor to Army or OSS service.
claims.match_notes: Modeled as professional affiliation because the reviewed source does not establish payroll status.

claims.claim_text: A 1928 federal appellate case identifies Robinson Verrill as a lawyer with Verrill, Hale, Booth & Ives in Portland, Maine.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The contemporary counsel listing names Robinson Verrill and the historical Portland law firm.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable match from the uncommon exact name and legal profession; Box 803 is required to close the identity bridge to the later lieutenant colonel.
claims.temporal_assessment: Definitely prewar, but too early to establish the firm as the immediate pre-OSS or last civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: Published with visible qualification and excluded from default confirmed/high employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Eliot N Vestner is high-confidence matched to Captain Eliot N. Vestner, the OSS Area A chief instructor in 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact uncommon name, indexed identifier, Army chronology and official NPS Area A role align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from exact full-name agreement, the indexed protected identifier and two concordant institutional histories.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish Army service beginning in December 1941 and an OSS training role in 1943.
claims.match_notes: The civilian employer before Army entry remains unidentified.

claims.claim_text: Eliot N. Vestner's best-supported immediate pre-OSS status is U.S. Army service begun in December 1941.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A local institutional history dates his Army entry to about two weeks after Pearl Harbor; the NPS places him in OSS Area A by 1943.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence Eliot N. Vestner identity.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate military pathway; the sources do not state the exact Army-to-OSS transfer date.
claims.match_notes: Military assignment, not a civilian employer. The claim remains visibly qualified.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Commander Frederick Vetlesen is confirmed as Cmdr. Frederick W. G. U. Vetlesen, USNR, in an official OSS awards-board record.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official record matches the uncommon indexed name, commander rank and Norwegian-Danish resistance mission.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed for the exact Frederick Vetlesen OSS record; the separate bridge to Columbia's Georg Unger Vetlesen remains probable rather than settled.
claims.temporal_assessment: The award record documents OSS wartime work, not the prewar civilian chronology.
claims.match_notes: The official spelling is preserved. The Columbia name variant is not silently substituted.

claims.claim_text: Columbia's institutional biography supports a probable prewar occupation for indexed Frederick Vetlesen as a shipbuilder in the United States.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Columbia describes Georg Unger Vetlesen as a successful U.S. shipbuilder who became a Navy commander and worked with Norwegian resistance during World War II.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable identity bridge from the highly distinctive Vetlesen surname, commander rank, Navy service and Norwegian-resistance mission; first names conflict.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented as prewar civilian work, but neither a named employer nor an exact immediate-to-Navy chronology is supplied.
claims.match_notes: Published only as a qualified occupation lead. Box 804 is required before treating Georg and Frederick as the same person for confirmed analytics.
